title: I actually shipped my first game using AI! It's a JRPG-inspired deckbuilder and already made 30 sales. Here's what I've learned.
author: Westwaage
selftext:
Hey everyone! I've been working on my first-ever game, Sunward Sentinel, and recently released it into Early Access on itch.io.

It's a JRPG-inspired tactical deckbuilder made in Godot, featuring 7 classes, 88 cards, a connected world map, 33 combat encounters, and 6 boss fights. I never got into games like Slay the Spire because I prefer playing games with full party members so I just made one myself.

AI has been central to the entire development process. I've primarily used Codex for programming, implementation, debugging, and testing, alongside AI image generation for some character artwork, animations, and visual effects.

One of the biggest things I've learned is how much iteration matters. Getting AI to produce something that technically works is one challenge. Getting it to look polished, animate consistently, and integrate properly with everything else can take quite a few rounds of revisions.

A recent example: I recently implemented a giant rattlesnake boss where the head and tail are independently targetable, and the tail can be killed and resurrected. Getting the different parts to animate together as one creature has been an interesting challenge! It's actually still not perfect and I need to ship out a correction for some of the visuals with it.

I'm excited that I've finally reached the point of shipping something playable. I used to start making games without ever getting them to be shipped in the past. Having AI enable me has been fun! There's still plenty I want to improve, but it's rewarding to see the project come together.

If anyone wants to check it out, here's the [itch.io](http://itch.io) page:

[https://gradientware.itch.io/sunward-sentinel](https://gradientware.itch.io/sunward-sentinel)

It's currently available for Windows at a discounted Early Access price of $5.99, which also includes the eventual full release.

Feedback on the combat, visuals, or overall gameplay would be very welcome!

comments.author: Express_Strength5253
comments.body: How'd you get the sprites to be so consistent?

comments.author: tuptain
comments.body: The backgrounds stand out to me, looks like the party is floating.

replies.author: Westwaage
replies.body: This is something I'm considering for the beta where I redesign the party formation and HUD panels to be more in line with an RPG like Octopath Traveler.

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: Congrats on the sales and all but I generally don’t get how this was ready to ship, you have characters who clearly aren’t supposed to be flying levitating above the ground….but again, congrats on the sales. I just don’t understand.

replies.author: Westwaage
replies.body: It was intended to be more of an isometric 2D RPG thing where the background is just for show and spatial cohesion isn't adhered to. But I'm considering moving the characters down and the HUDs above them to the sides to make it more like Octopath Traveler.

replies.author: Braunb8888
replies.body: I’d heavily advise that but hey, you’re selling, so who knows.

replies.author: Westwaage
replies.body: It's only in Alpha so I can iterate for the Beta and final versions as much as I'd like. Let me know in chat if you'd like a free Itch download key if you'd be willing to provide feedback because I'd like more playtesters. Most of the buyers right now aren't engaging back... which is fine for them I guess lol.

comments.author: Significant_Tell407
comments.body: Idk i feel like this is one of those cases where you could have had something good by investing more time. Its inspired clearly by Baten Kaitos but has none of the charm. The ui and world looks so generic. The world map is just a copy and pasted chatgpt image. What you need to do is take 1 building and create a cohesive art style. The use that image as a reference to make your game identifiable.

replies.author: Westwaage
replies.body: It's only in Alpha so I'm still iterating. There were people who wanted to buy it in its current state and still have access to the Beta and final versions. I can definitely take this feedback into account for the next release. Also, a lot of the art is currently just a placeholder.

comments.author: Joe_Capello
comments.body: How long did this take you?
